scope: VCF sample versus genome representation, sample mixture examples, PEDIGREE header syntax, clonal derivation and haplotype identity corresponding to VCFv4.5 tables VCF5.42 and VCF5.43.

deltas.finding: The target genome identifier moves into the explicit ID attribute; the old Name_0 field is replaced by ID=SampleID. Parent/ancestor relationships remain conceptually the same. The specification's recommendation to represent derivation relationships in PEDIGREE remains a recommendation.

changes.finding: DPADJ, CNADJ and CICNADJ are removed in the VCFv4.4 change log.
The sample mixture examples replace FORMAT DPADJ with AD and CNADJ with CN.
INFO CN becomes allele-specific copy number and FORMAT CN becomes total copy number for the sample; do not treat CNADJ and CN as semantically interchangeable.

persistent_semantics.sample_genome_distinction: Present in all five versions; sample metadata can describe multiple genomes/mixtures and should not be conflated with the genome-level biological entity. See the version section locators above.
persistent_semantics.clonal_derivation: PEDIGREE supports derived/original and parent/ancestor genome relationships; the syntax changes in VCFv4.3 as described.
persistent_semantics.mutation_quality_score: The text discusses representing uncertainty about when a variant arose due to insufficient data or sample mixtures in all five versions; preserve its exact normative/recommendation status and do not invent a scoring algorithm.
persistent_semantics.haplotype: A haplotype is a set of variants known to be on the same chromosome in the germline genome; identifiers are unique across the germline genome and conserved along clonal lineages despite mutation/rearrangement/recombination. Duplication creates novel haplotypes while retaining one original ID; these novel haplotypes share a haplotype ancestor in the parent genome. This text is present in all five versions.

table_interpretation.VCF5_42: Sample/genome mixture and copy-number examples are informative; the surrounding prose defines sample/genome distinction and describes possible deconvolution, not a mandatory deconvolution algorithm.
table_interpretation.VCF5_43: PEDIGREE and haplotype examples illustrate the syntax and lineage model; preserve the recommendation/requirement force in the prose.

remaining: Independent reviewer must verify PEDIGREE syntax grammar and whether header values are constrained by sample identifiers or genome identifiers in each version.
Map the old-to-new PEDIGREE syntax migration, removal of DPADJ/CNADJ/CICNADJ and CN semantic changes to atomic requirement IDs.

Add positive/negative tests for old/new PEDIGREE syntax by version, parent/ancestor cardinality, sample/genome distinction, removed tags, AD/CN sample mixture records and haplotype identity/duplication.
No implementation or test execution is claimed.
